otherProblems: Sample and empty values both show the same generic placeholder logo for every sponsor, so the three-logo rotation can only be inferred from the dot indicator moving; the very wide wordmark named in the brief is never shown, so its fit cannot be judged.
The kicker 'CON EL APOYO DE' is small (about 20 px caps on a 1080 frame); acceptable for a secondary label on a deliberately small card but at the lower limit for television.

Mid-transition on Next (G-25, 300 ms) the logo well goes almost empty for a beat while the plate crossfades from white to dark; a viewer sees a brief dark blank well, not a cut, but it is a slightly ungraceful swap.
answer.reasons: A compact, opaque bottom-right card: orange header with dark 'CON EL APOYO DE', an inset logo well that switches between a white plate (sample logo) and a dark navy plate (white shield in the long-value frames) so both black and white wordmarks stay readable, and a three-dot rotation indicator. It holds up unchanged on the video, light and busy grounds, nothing is clipped or overlapped, the Take and Out are clean, and Hold, Next and Resume all behave as expected (the active dot advances on Resume at 10 s and stays put on Hold). The adaptive well is a legitimate design response to the brief's white/black logos rather than a stray logo box. Plain but balanced and readable; it would go to air as delivered.

otherProblems: When the map-name field is empty (all sample-value frames, e.g. G-2, G-23, G-41, G-75) a small empty dark stub remains at the left of the phase tab under the centre block; next to the red/orange/white phase tabs it reads as a tiny leftover block.

With the long values (G-5/G-6/G-7, crop G-89) the centre block says 'MAP 1' while the map tab below says 'MAP 3 · ANCIENT' – the bug keeps its own map counter separate from the free-text map field, so the two can contradict each other on air.
Pressing Next map directly after the Take (G-35–G-40) produces no visible change; it appears gated behind Map final, which is defensible, but no frame actually shows the map counter advancing.

Both logos sit on their own contrast tiles (dark tile for the pale logo, pale tile for the burgundy crest); it is a deliberate, well-integrated answer to the contrast problem the brief raises, but it is a plate under a logo.
answer.reasons: A clean, readable, well-balanced top-centre scorebug: team names wrap to two lines and stay inside their fields even with the long stress names, scores and MAP/BEST OF 3 are crisp, the Finnish phase tab changes colour sensibly for live, pause and final, and team-colour accents are aligned and tidy. Nothing overlaps, clips or becomes unreadable on the light or busy grounds. The only things a designer would pick at are the small empty stub left of the phase tab when no map name is set and the possible MAP 1 / MAP 3 contradiction under stress values – nits rather than reasons to hold it.

otherProblems: The logo well is dark navy; a white wordmark reads well (G-5/6/7) but no frame shows the black wordmark the brief mentions, so its legibility on that well cannot be confirmed.
Logos sit fairly small inside the well (shield in G-5 fills roughly a fifth of the well width), leaving generous empty space around them.
At 120 ms into the Take (G-12) the card briefly appears as an empty dark box with only the dots before the kicker and logo well fade in — a transient state a viewer would barely register.
answer.reasons: A compact, opaque navy card in the bottom-right with an orange top accent, a bold white 'CON EL APOYO DE' kicker, a three-dot rotation indicator and a centred logo well. The card is fully opaque so the kicker and logos stay readable on the video, light and busy grounds alike; nothing clips or escapes, including the long-value state and the native crops. Hold, Next and Resume all behave as the dots show (Hold stays on 1, Next advances, Resume continues after a Hold), and Take/Out are clean fades. The layout is balanced and the furniture is minimal, so it airs as delivered; the only reservations are the unverified black wordmark on a dark well and somewhat small logos.

otherProblems: Empty-values state (G-6/G-7) is inconsistent: the home row falls back to 'Domácí' while the away row shows only a crest with a blank name field, the period columns vanish entirely, and the clock reads '0:00' in blue — a viewer would not normally see this, but the fallback should be symmetrical.
The period column headers change from '1 2 3' (sample) to '1. 2. 3.' (long values), so the header labels are evidently data-driven rather than fixed furniture; a small consistency nit.
In the sample state the 2 and 3 period cells are left blank rather than dashed; acceptable but a touch unfinished-looking before those periods are played.

During the Take (G-14, G-15) the header title and the away score are seen partially masked mid-slide; this reads as an intentional reveal animation, not a settled-frame clip, but it is a slightly abrupt reveal.
answer.reasons: A clean, compact white/ice-blue top-left scoreboard with everything the brief asks for: both crests on their own tiles proportionate to the text, club names, big scores in a tinted column, period label, clock, and a per-period goals grid. The long Czech names with diacritics ('HC Slavoj Žďár nad Sázavou', 'HC Spartak Frýdek-Místek') fit their fields with margin in every settled frame and in the native crops, nothing overlaps, and contrast is strong on both video and light grounds. All five required operator actions are present and visibly work: the clock counts down and freezes on stop, reset returns it to 20:00, intermission swaps the clock for a 'PŘESTÁVKA' badge, resume restores the clock, and final turns the header navy with 'KONEC ZÁPASU'. The only blemishes are in the empty-values stress state and some minor label inconsistency, none of which a viewer would see in a real game.

A: Logo well is dark navy in every frame (A-2, A-5, A-16, A-27); the grey element of the placeholder logo in A-2/A-4 is already low-contrast on it, so the card gives no evidence it can carry a dark wordmark the brief calls for
Pager dots are small and sit tight against the top-right corner of the label row (A-2) — a nit a viewer would barely notice
B: B-13 (Take, 300 ms): 'CON EL APOYO DE' is seen half-masked behind the header during the reveal — transition only, settled frames are clean
The white outline, solid orange header and dark footer make the card read a little heavy and device-like against the plate (B-2, B-4); not a mistake, just less refined than it could be
Black label text on orange header has no accent tie to the rest of the card's palette — stylistic, not a fault

answer.reasons: Both cards sit cleanly in the bottom-right, keep the label legible over the video, light and busy grounds, hold the long shield logo and the empty state inside the well, and show the pager advancing on Take, Next and Resume with clean cross-fades, so both would air. B is preferred for this brief because its logo well visibly adapts to the logo it carries — white behind the coloured/grey placeholder (B-2, B-4) and dark behind the white shield (B-5, B-7) — which is exactly what a rotation of a white, a black and a wide wordmark over a crowded finish-line shot needs; A keeps a single dark well throughout, which suits the white logo but offers no shown answer for the black one and already lets the grey placeholder element go dim. A is the tidier piece of design, but B's one visible rough edge is a reveal-animation frame, not a settled-state fault.

A: A-13.jpg (Take at 300 ms): the kicker 'CON EL APOYO DE' is briefly half-masked while it slides up into the orange header — a reveal wipe, settled cleanly by 600 ms, but a strict eye sees text under a mask for a moment
The card stacks three tones (orange header, dark body, white logo tile plus a pale stroke) and reads a touch heavy for a small corner sponsor card
B: The logo well is a fixed dark navy in every frame (B-2, B-5, B-39); the only non-placeholder logo shown is the white shield, so nothing in the frames demonstrates how a black wordmark would survive on it
B-12.jpg (Take at 120 ms): the panel is up with its three dots but no kicker and no logo for a beat — a momentary empty box during the build

answer.reasons: Both cards sit cleanly in the bottom-right, carry 'CON EL APOYO DE' legibly on the video, light and busy grounds, and the frames show the rotation advancing (dots move at 10 s), hold keeping the logo, skip advancing it and resume restarting — nothing clipped, nothing empty in a settled state. A is the one I'd rather air for a sponsor slot: its logo tile is a proper white well that flips to dark for the white shield (A-5/A-52), which is the visible answer to a brief that insists a white and a black wordmark both stay readable over a colourful finish line. B is the more refined object — single navy tone, orange hairline, dots tucked beside the kicker — but it only ever shows logos on dark navy, which is the riskier home for sponsor artwork. Neither has a basic mistake; A's half-masked kicker at 300 ms is a reveal wipe, not a stuck clip.

otherProblems: In the reveal (G-26–G-28, G-33) the dark 'THE WINNER' tab sits tight on the top edge of the gold band and very close above the winner's name; it reads as designed but the stack is a little crowded.
The reveal band at 20 ms (G-23) briefly overshoots wider than the nominee rows before settling; a transitional frame a viewer would barely register.
answer.reasons: A clean, centred black-and-gold nominees board: small gold kicker, serif category, gold rule with diamond, four evenly spaced rows with director over film title. Long category and long names all fit on one line inside the panel (G-5–G-7, G-44/45), and the near-opaque panel keeps everything readable over the light and busy grounds. Suspense dims the nominees, reveal drops a gold band with a 'THE WINNER' tab over the winner and greys out the rest, with no text collisions or clipping; empty values fall back to just the category title, and the Out fades cleanly. Nothing a director would hold it for.

otherProblems: The panel is slightly translucent, so a busy or bright plate (G-4, G-7, G-10) shows faintly through the black; text stays readable but a fully opaque plate would be safer over the LED wall.
Empty-values state (G-8/9/10) falls back to a bare 'BEST SHORT FILM' title with no eyebrow, inconsistent with the populated board; a no-data edge case only.
Bottom padding of the panel is a little deeper than the top; a nit a viewer would not notice.
answer.reasons: A clean, centred black-and-gold nominees board: gold eyebrow, large white serif category, a short gold rule, and four name/title pairs separated by hairlines, all with generous margins. Long names and the two-line long category stay inside the panel without clipping or collision (G-5–G-7, G-38, G-44). Suspense dims the nominees and pulses the frame; Reveal highlights the winner on a gold band with the others dimmed (G-26–G-28), so both required actions work and are legible. Text is readable on every ground, nothing overlaps, and the take/out animations settle to the same board.

A: Reveal (A-27/A-28) is understated: a faint gold band and gold-tinted name, with no winner label; readable but easy to miss as a reveal moment.
Long category wraps to two lines at reduced size (A-5, A-34–38); clean but busier than a single line.
Transient animation frames (A-23 band wider than the rows, A-25 outline box around the winner row) differ from the settled look — not settled-state faults.
B: "THE WINNER" tab sits tight between the diamond ornament and the winner's name (B-27/B-28) — clears both, but with little breathing room.
Reveal band overshoots the row width briefly at 20 ms (B-23) before settling; a transient animation state only.
Secondary title line in spaced small caps is on the small side for a television, though still legible.

answer.reasons: Both graphics are clean, centred black-and-gold boards with no text overlaps, no clipping, and full legibility over the video, light and busy grounds, including the long-value stress frames. Both offer the brief's suspense and reveal steps and each step shows what it should. B is the stronger board for an awards night: the gold winner band with a 'THE WINNER' tab reads instantly, the long category holds on one line, the row cards give the list structure, and the panel padding is even. A airs but its reveal is quiet (a tinted name and faint band) and the long category has to wrap to two lines.

A: A-23: during the reveal's first frames the gold winner band is briefly wider than the nominee rows before it settles (A-25 onward) — a transient only, not a viewer-visible fault once settled.
B: B-5/B-6/B-7/B-34–B-38: the long category wraps to two lines with a single orphan word ('DIRECTOR') on the second line — contained and readable, but it reads as untidy next to the single-line title in A.

B-23–B-28: the winner highlight is a subtle gold tint band with the name turned gold; it is visible but noticeably less emphatic than a reveal moment calls for, and the band pulses between widths (B-27 vs B-28).
B-45: native crop of the kicker field includes the top of the category glyphs beneath it, suggesting a tight field box — not visible in any full frame.

answer.reasons: Both boards are clean black-and-gold centred panels: no text overlaps, nothing cut or spilling in the stress frames, long names and the long category stay inside their fields, both offer suspense and reveal and the steps do what the brief needs, and the out fades cleanly. A is the stronger one on air: the stress category fits on one line, the nominee rows sit in evenly spaced panels, suspense dims the field clearly, and the reveal turns the winner into a full gold band with a 'THE WINNER' tag, which reads instantly from across a room. B is competent but quieter — its long category breaks into two lines with an orphan word, and its reveal is a gentle tint that a viewer could miss against a bright LED wall. Both would go to air; A is the one I'd put up for an awards reveal.

otherProblems: With details and source left empty (G-8/9/10) the panel keeps its full height, leaving the lower ~40% of the dark strap blank under the headline; the brief always fills these fields, so a viewer is unlikely to see it, but the strap does not collapse to fit.
The source line (~24 px grey caps) is on the small side for a television, though still legible against the dark panel.
answer.reasons: A clean, conventional alert strap: a solid colour level tag on the left, dark panel carrying bold headline, details and source, with a matching accent line across the top. All four levels are offered and change colour unmistakably (yellow, orange, red, magenta) with tag text that stays readable on each, and the levels step back down cleanly (G-51–56). Text is fully legible over the video, light and busy grounds because it sits on the opaque dark panel. The long headline wraps to two lines and fits within the panel, and the native crops confirm the long details and source are not clipped. The Take and Out animate without leaving anything broken on screen. Nothing a viewer would see keeps it off air.

otherProblems: Empty-values frames (G-8, G-9, G-10): with details and source blank the panel keeps its full height, leaving the headline at the top of a large empty black band — reads as broken if an operator ever airs it without details/source.

Badge label and level colour appear to be driven separately: the long-values set (G-5–G-7) shows 'AVISO' in advisory yellow, while the Warning step (G-29–G-34) shows 'AVISO' in red — a label/colour mismatch is possible.

Level wording is questionable for a South Texas NWS context: Advisory is labelled ADVERTENCIA and Warning is labelled AVISO, which is the reverse of the NWS Spanish convention (Aviso = Advisory, Advertencia = Warning); a viewer who knows the terms may read the escalation backwards.
Details and source lines are on the small side for a television (~28 px and ~22 px), though still legible over the opaque panel.
Take animation reveals the headline through a horizontal wipe (G-13 shows it half-clipped at 300 ms) — a normal reveal, but a brief, visible clip during the Take.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-balanced strap: a solid colour badge keyed to the level, an opaque dark panel with bold two-line headline, details and source, and a matching accent rule. All four operator actions work and the colour change (yellow → orange → red → magenta) is clear at every step, including stepping back down. The long headline, details and source all fit inside their fields without clipping, and the panel stays legible over the busy and light grounds. The weaknesses are edge cases — the panel does not collapse when details/source are empty, and the badge wording/colour coupling looks unreliable — but with normal values nothing a viewer would see keeps it off air.

A: A-8/A-9/A-10 (empty values): headline sits at the top of a fixed-height panel with a large blank area below it — only visible if details and source are left empty.
A-5/A-6/A-7 (long values): details line drops to a noticeably smaller size with a wider gap to the headline; readable but small on a TV.
B: B-8/B-9/B-10 (empty values): same fixed-height panel with the headline pushed to the top and a blank area below.
B-5/B-6/B-7 (long values): details line drops to a small size with a wider gap, same as A.
B-12 to B-16 and settled frames: a faint soft shadow band on the dark panel at the join with the level tab (x≈450–480), barely visible but slightly smears an otherwise crisp edge.

answer.reasons: Both straps are essentially the same design and both air: a solid level tab that switches cleanly yellow → orange → red → magenta (and back down in the 51–56 frames), white headline/details/source on a dark panel that stays legible over the video, light and busy grounds, long headlines wrapping to two lines inside the panel, and all four operator levels present and working. Neither has text over text, clipping in a settled frame, or illegible text; the only mid-glyph cut is the designed mask reveal at 300 ms during the Take, identical in both. The differences are tiny: B carries a faint shadow smear where the tab meets the panel, while A's join is crisp, so A edges it on fewer visible blemishes; the shared weak spots are the top-pushed headline in the empty-values state and the small details type when values are long.

A: A-5/A-6/A-7: with long values the details line auto-shrinks and leaves a visibly larger gap above the source line than in the sample frames (minor, in bounds).
A-8/A-9/A-10: with empty details/source the strap keeps full height, so the headline sits at the top of a mostly empty dark panel (stress case only).
B: B-3/B-6/B-9: the dark strap carries a warm tinted gradient that reads slightly muddy/olive on the light ground; still legible.
B-5/B-6/B-7: with long values the gap between headline and details is larger than between details and source, so the stack reads slightly uneven (minor, in bounds).
B-8/B-9/B-10: with empty details/source the strap keeps full height, so the headline sits at the top of a mostly empty dark panel (stress case only).

answer.reasons: Both graphics are the same design: a level badge on the left, a dark strap with headline, details and source, and an accent rule that recolours with the badge. Both change colour clearly and distinctly at advisory, watch, warning and emergency, lower back to advisory cleanly, carry the long headline on two lines without clipping (crops confirm), stay legible over the video, light and busy grounds, and animate in and out without text left on screen. No basic mistakes in either; the 300 ms take frame is a deliberate masked slide-up reveal in both. A edges it only because its strap is a neutral charcoal that stays clean on every ground, while B's strap has a warm tinted gradient that looks a little muddy on the light plate; otherwise they are near-identical, hence low confidence in the preference.

otherProblems: The operator surface folds 'hold' into holdFi/holdSv (jump-and-hold) rather than offering a standalone freeze of whichever language is currently up; the brief's described workflow (jump to a language, hold, resume) is still fully achievable.
With empty values (G-6/G-7) the band keeps its full height with only the heading in it, leaving a largely empty panel — a stress case, not a brief state.
answer.reasons: A calm, well-proportioned civic band: dark navy panel with a thin gold top rule, a tidy FI/SV badge stack whose active language is highlighted, a gold heading and white body at a size that reads on a television. Both the sample and the long Finnish values wrap cleanly onto two lines well inside the panel with no clipping, overlap or contrast problems on the video or light grounds; the native crops confirm clean glyphs. Take, Out, Suomi, Svenska and Alternate states all render correctly, the badge swaps with the language, and the surface lets the operator jump to either language, hold it, and resume alternation as the brief asks.

otherProblems: Automatic alternation is never demonstrated: both the Take and the Resume sequences still show Finnish at 10 000 ms, so the self-alternation the brief asks for can only be inferred, not seen (the interval may simply be longer than 10 s).

With empty values (G-6/G-7) the heading falls back to a default title and the band keeps its full height with a large blank area beneath it; an operator would not air this state, but it reads as an empty block.
Long-side-2 frames (G-10/G-11) show the Finnish side, so the Swedish text's behaviour with long values is never shown.
The language indicator dots are very small; the active/inactive state is carried mostly by the text weight and colour, which is adequate but subtle.
answer.reasons: A calm, well-proportioned navy band in the lower third with a single orange accent bar, a clear eyebrow heading, two readable body lines, a thin rule and a footer, plus a tidy SUOMI/SVENSKA indicator that switches state with the language. Long values stay inside the panel on two lines, nothing collides with the indicator or the rule, contrast is good on both grounds, and the Take, language switches, Hold, Resume, Update and Out all transition cleanly. Lang1, lang2, hold and resume are all present on the surface and the language buttons visibly change the content. The only reservation is that the automatic alternation itself is not caught within the 10 s frames, but no frame shows anything wrong.

A: Operator surface offers holdFi/holdSv/resume only: there is no plain 'hold' of whatever language is currently showing, so the operator must know which side is up and pick the right button or the language flips (brief lists hold as a separate action).
No frame ever shows the self-alternation happening: Take at 10000 ms (A-13) and Alternate at 10000 ms (A-31, A-47) still show Finnish; Swedish only appears via the explicit Svenska button.
Empty-values state (A-6, A-7) leaves a wide band with only the heading and the badge column, right two-thirds hollow (empty state only).
B: Empty-values state (B-6, B-7) leaves a tall band with only the kicker heading and the language switch, the rest of the panel and the footer gone (empty state only).
Take frames at 120–300 ms (B-13, B-14) show the divider rule drawn before any text arrives; a 300 ms transition artefact a viewer would barely register.
Kicker heading is small, tracked uppercase; readable on a TV but close to the floor.

answer.reasons: Both bands are clean, readable and balanced: dark navy plates along the bottom, long Finnish and Swedish values fit on two lines, nothing clipped or overlapping, transitions fade in and out without artefacts. B is the one to air for this brief: its operator surface matches the four actions the brief asks for exactly, every step (Language 1, Language 2, Hold, Resume, then Resume after a hold) does what it should, and the 10 s Take frame (B-17) actually shows the notice crossing to Svenska on its own with the SUOMI/SVENSKA indicator lighting the live side. A works and would air, but its surface folds hold into holdFi/holdSv with no plain hold, and across every frame it never alternates by itself, so the brief's core behaviour is only demonstrated by B.

A: A-6.jpg / A-7.jpg (empty values): the band keeps its default heading and language toggle over a large empty body/footer area — a half-empty panel, though only in the empty-values stress case.
A-2.jpg: the SUOMI/SVENSKA toggle and the PORVOON KAUPUNKI · BORGÅ STAD footer are set small (caps ~20 px); readable on a TV but at the lower limit.

B: Operator surface: the brief needs lang1, lang2, hold and resume; B offers only holdFi, holdSv and resume. There is no standalone hold (freeze whatever is showing) and no plain jump without hold — the jump and hold are fused into holdFi/holdSv, so the named actions the brief requires are not all offered.

B-2.jpg: the FI/SV language pills sit in their own column with a vertical rule beside them — small decorative furniture a civic band does not strictly need, though it does not collide with text.

answer.reasons: Both bands are clean, readable and balanced in every settled, long-value and light-ground frame; neither has text clipping, overlap, contrast failures or transition glitches worth refusing on. The decisive difference is the operator surface: A exposes exactly lang1, lang2, hold and resume, and the frames show each doing its job (jump to Finnish, jump to Swedish with the toggle lighting SVENSKA, hold, resume). B collapses the four needed actions into holdFi/holdSv/resume, so a standalone hold (and a plain language jump) is not offered as the brief lists it — as delivered, the desk cannot drive it the way the brief asks. B's gold-rule/pill design is handsome and would otherwise air, and its small Out artefact is a nit, but A is the one I would put on air for this brief.

basicMistakes.where: Focus skier step: the full tower (G-17 to G-22, through 10000 ms) is pixel-identical to the settled board in G-2/G-15 — no row is highlighted, dimmed, enlarged or isolated. The focused-row state the brief needs never appears in any frame, and the follow-up 'Whole field after Focus' frames (G-51 to G-56) are likewise unchanged, so the focus/clear pair does nothing on screen.

missingActions: focus (offered on the surface, but produces no visible focused row in any frame)
otherProblems: DNF row is inconsistent between data sets: sample values show only the DNF badge (G-2), long values show a '–' dash plus the badge (G-5).
When the OFFISIELT badge appears (G-33) the name column and gap column shift left/right by a few pixels compared with G-27, a small reflow a viewer might notice on the cut.
Empty-values state (G-8 to G-10) leaves a bare accent rule under the title with nothing beneath it — not a brief value, but it reads slightly unfinished.
answer.reasons: The static design is clean and broadcast-ready: dark panel at left over the course camera, readable white names with Norwegian characters, right-aligned gaps, leader in red, DNF row dimmed with a badge, long session title and long double-barrelled names all fit, and the Final step adds a tidy OFFISIELT badge that Provisional removes. But the brief's core live action — focusing the row of the skier the commentator is talking about — shows nothing: every Focus frame is identical to the whole-field board, so the operator cannot do the one thing the brief asks for during commentary. As delivered, a director would have no focus state to put on air, so it does not go out today.

otherProblems: In the long-values state (G-5/6/7) the row for 'Mathias Kristoffersen Haugland' drops to a noticeably smaller condensed size than the other rows, so one row visibly differs in weight; readable but it will catch an eye.

In the long-values state the gap column right-aligns to about x=622 while the DNF badge sits at the panel edge (x≈697), so the times hang ~95px short of the right padding and a stray '–' sits beside the DNF badge; a small alignment inconsistency a viewer may half-notice.
Empty-values state (G-8/9/10) shows only the title and the red rule with a blank band where the subtitle would be; acceptable as a fallback but reads slightly unfinished.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-structured timing tower: dark opaque panel sits top-left over the course camera, white names and gaps are readable on every ground including the busy one, Norwegian letters render correctly, and the DNF row is clearly demoted with an outlined badge. Focus dims the field and marks the chosen row with a red left accent that stays clear of the text; clear restores the field; final adds a tidy FINAL badge in the header; provisional removes it. Long names are held in bounds (one row by shrinking, the title by fitting) without clipping or overlap, and the in/out transitions are brief and tidy. The stress-state font shrink and the shifted gap column are small nits, not reasons to keep it off air.

A: A-5/A-6/A-7 (long values): row 2 'Mathias Kristoffersen Haugland' is auto-shrunk to a visibly smaller type size than every other row, so one line reads differently from the rest of the tower.

A-5/A-6/A-7 (long values): the gap column slides left (values end ~75 px short of where they sit in A-2) while the DNF badge stays at the right edge, so the right side of the panel reads ragged; a stray '–' also sits beside the DNF badge.
Minor: busy-ground frames (A-4/A-7) rely on the panel's opacity; readable but the plate is dark enough only just.
B: Basic mistake – Focus never appears: the 'Focus skier' settled frames B-19, B-20, B-21, B-22 are pixel-identical to the plain on-air state (B-2, B-15) – row 1 already wears the red badge by default and no row is highlighted, dimmed or set apart – so the focus the brief needs is shown in no frame; 'Whole field' (B-23–B-28, B-51–B-56) is likewise unchanged, so focus and clear are visually no-ops.
B-5/B-6/B-7 (long values): stray '–' glyph next to the DNF badge on the DNF row.
Minor: a lighter grey shadow strip shows under the panel's bottom edge on the light ground (B-3, B-9).

answer.reasons: A does what the brief asks: it takes in cleanly, the Focus step clearly isolates the chosen skier (red tick, others dimmed), Whole field restores the tower, and Final adds a tidy FINAL badge that Provisional removes. Its only real flaws are in the long-name stress state, where one row shrinks to a smaller size and the gap column drifts left of the DNF badge – noticeable to a designer but not enough to pull it. B is the more handsomely built panel and carries the long names at full size with a clean right edge, but its Focus and Whole-field buttons produce no visible change at all – the focused state the commentator depends on never appears in any frame – so it cannot do the job as delivered. A airs; B does not.

A: A-17.jpg through A-22.jpg (Focus skier after the Take, all timings): pressing Focus produces no visible change at all — the board is identical to the whole-field state (A-15/A-16). The focused row the brief needs never appears in any frame.
